incident.name: Pantanal wetland-savanna, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil/Bolivia border
incident.description: August 2024 dry-season fire activity in the Pantanal, part of the record 2024 South American fire season.
incident.why_chosen: Savanna/grassland dry-season spread with a long-lived multi-day fire front, in a different hemisphere and fuel type from the Canadian cases.

availability.note: init day present, >= 3 following days with VIIRS cell-days in the window, observed new cells > 0

init.semantics: forecast uses fire detections through the end of this UTC day and nothing later

method.description: XGBoost direct multi-horizon ML (equifire.direct) blended with Rothermel/minimum-travel-time physics (backend.ensemble.predict); 'ml' rows score the same ML component alone.

model.inputs: VIIRS history plus MODIS activity features

method.scoring: cumulative cells newly burning by day k inside the 41x41-cell window; strict = same 0.05 deg cell; tolerant = within 1 cell (~5.5 km), same as walk_forward._tol

leakage_audit.fire_observations: as-of index: all cell-days after 2024-08-20 removed before forecasting (max day in forecaster input = 2024-08-20)
leakage_audit.weather: physics uses ERA5 reanalysis for the forecast period (perfect-weather); ML uses init-day weather only

issued.hourly_simulation_note: same machinery run from the init time; recomputed live, uses the full archive and reanalysis weather
warnings: Experimental blend: measured gains over ML alone are not established.
Physics burned fraction is not an ignition probability; low/high are scenario envelopes.
The hourly landscape simulation is a separate richer model, not the physics used to fit this blender.
Physics uses observed archive weather: historical replay, not a forecast-weather backtest.

class_definitions.hit: predicted and observed new burning cell (strict, same 0.05 deg cell)
class_definitions.miss: observed new burning cell that was not predicted
class_definitions.false_alarm: predicted cell with no observed burning, in a place/day with a usable overpass proxy
class_definitions.unverifiable: predicted cell with no observed burning, but no clear overpass proxy (cloud) so absence of detection is not evidence of no fire
class_definitions.near_hit: tolerant view only: not a strict hit but matched with an observed/predicted cell within 1 cell (~5.5 km)

reveal.truth_definition: cumulative cells NOT burning on the init day, detected by VIIRS (NOAA-20/21/S-NPP) on a later day <= k and within k cells of the burning area (same as walk_forward case_truth)

limitations: Physics uses ERA5 reanalysis weather for the forecast period (perfect-weather replay): physics skill is optimistic vs a real-time forecast that only has weather forecasts. The ML component uses only day-of-init weather.
Fire observations after the end of the init UTC day are removed from the forecaster's input (as-of index); forecast models were trained on years before the incident year (walk-forward folds).
'Truth' is satellite detection (VIIRS 375 m, 0.05 deg cells), not burned perimeter: absence of detection is not proof of no fire (clouds, smoke, overpass gaps, fire below detection threshold).

The cloud/overpass caveat is a proxy from ERA5 modelled cloud cover at nominal local overpass times; actual overpass schedules and swath coverage are not reconstructed. Unverifiable cells are reported separately.

Scores come from single events, not a benchmark: the 100-fire/year walk-forward in forecast.py is the statistically meaningful measure. Curated incidents were chosen for diversity, so they are illustrative.
Probabilities are uncalibrated and the physics burned fraction is not an ignition probability.
2023 and earlier incidents can only be replayed ML-only (no ML+physics blender exists for them).
